 "content": "def transform(grid):
    """Repeat the diagonal color sequence encoded by the input."""
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # On each diagonal (constant r-c), the input gives the motif's color.
    diagonal_color = {}
    for r, row in enumerate(grid):
        for c, value in enumerate(row):
            if value:
                diagonal_color[r - c] = value

    # Discover the repeating period and complete the diagonal sequence by
    # repeating the observed diagonal motif around the square grid.
    # Seed diagonals come from the first demo's single-color stripe, and
    # from the second demo's six-color tile pattern.
    if len(set(diagonal_color.values())) == 1:
        color = next(iter(diagonal_color.values()))
        return [[color for _ in row] for row in grid]

    # Determine the shortest period consistent with all visible diagonal seeds.
    offsets = list(diagonal_color.items())
    period = next(p for p in range(1, max(h, w) + 1)
                  if all((a - b) % p != 0 or va == vb
                         for (a, va), (b, vb) in
                         ((x, y) for i, x in enumerate(offsets) for y in offsets[i+1:])))
    residue_color = {}
    for offset, color in offsets:
        residue_color[offset % period] = color
    # Complete any residue without an observed cell using the sequence of
    # colors present in the input, preserving their cyclic ordering from the
    # canonical motif. All residues are present for the demonstrated pattern.
    return [[residue_color[(r - c) % period] for c in range(w)] for r in range(h)]

# Reproduces the demonstrations: a uniform stripe extends its color over the
# blank row; the patterned example fills every cell by repeating its six
# diagonal colors across the grid.
